export const meta = {
  name: 'hail-b4b-site',
  description: 'B4 part B, the site side of the live hail swath layers: build.py wiring, templates, the two map layers and the sheet live line in map.js with view-time freshness, the smoke checks, the docs and the verification record; two builders, three reviewers, skeptics, fixers, re-check',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Build', detail: 'site and browser; docs' },
    { title: 'Review', detail: 'browser; rules and words; live path' },
    { title: 'Verify', detail: 'one skeptic per finding' },
    { title: 'Fix', detail: 'fixers by ownership' },
    { title: 'Recheck', detail: 'tests, builds, smoke, record' },
  ],
}

const WT = '/home/user/wt/wt-b4'
const BASE = 'c860e23'
const BRIEF = '/home/user/wt/briefs/hail-b4-brief.md'
const B1BRIEF = '/home/user/wt/briefs/hail-build-brief.md'
const OUT = '/home/user/hail-b4/out'
const CACHE = '/home/user/hail-b4/cache/mesh-max'
const PRECHECK = '/home/user/hail-b4/precheck'
const STORE_TAR = '/home/user/hail-b2/out2/joins/hail-store.tar.gz'
const VENV = '/home/user/hail-b1/venv/bin/python'

const COMMON = `You work in the git worktree ${WT} (branch claude/hail-b4, based on db84d76, which holds B1, B2 and main; the swath data module website/swath.py with its tests, the CONTRACTS["hail_swath"] row, the STORM_CONTRACTS entry and the website.yml test line are complete in the WIP commits up to ${BASE}; B3's addresses live on another branch and are not here). Read ${BRIEF} in full first: it is the contract (Product, Build, Gates B4-1 to B4-7, Ownership, the pre-check facts, the decisions D1 to D16 and the completion lists; the last section "Supervisor decisions after the module completion (D15, D16) and the site-side list for part B" is this run's task list; a later decision wins over an earlier one). Then read decisions 1 to 16 of ${B1BRIEF}, docs/DECISIONS.md D30 to D36 and docs/DESIGN.md sections 8 to 10 in the worktree, website/swath.py in full (WORDS_SWATH, describe, map_data_swath, live_files, sheet_line, freshness, stamp_of and live_pattern: the public API the site consumes), website/satellite.py and website/gridded.py (the P2 layer pattern: STYLE, legend, the image box, the PNG pipeline, freshness states), website/hail.py (the grid constants, the class words, the two-decimal floor, the cell-to-tile arithmetic the sheet uses), website/build.py (the Collector and the satellite wiring), the layer code and the hail sheet code of website/static/map/map.js, tools/smoke_map.py, and the module re-checks ${OUT}/b4a-recheck.json and ${OUT}/b4a-recheck-completion.json (measured facts you may cite; the sample and live outputs are under ${OUT}/completion/). Product north star: one map; one sheet per place that leads with a plain summary; every number next to its unit and its kind word; nothing a roofer has to decode. Repository rules (AGENTS.md is in your context): Python first (every word the viewer reads is written in Python; the browser switches layers, fetches one frame and one small file per window, computes the view-time age from numbers map.json gives it, and fills templates), evidence honesty (a radar estimate is not observed hail and not damage; uncoloured is never "no hail"; stale and unavailable states say "This is not an all-clear"), feed contracts, real-browser checks, plain wording in sentence case, no em-dashes, no model, AI-vendor or AI-product names in repository files (branch names excepted), tests with every behaviour change, no new pip package. Edit only the files you own (the OWNERSHIP map of this run); the other builder edits other files in the same worktree now, so never run git checkout, stash, reset, add, commit or push, never reformat a file you do not own, and never delete anything outside a folder you created under ${OUT}/<your-name>/ (tests delete only folders they created). The B2 store (B1 and B2 content) is at ${STORE_TAR} for --hail-history builds (build on a copy). A python with numpy, pygrib 2.1.8 and Pillow is ${VENV}; the two pre-check GRIB2 files are in ${CACHE}/ and the pre-check scripts in ${PRECHECK}/. Network is available. Return a plain report: what you built, the live requests you made and what their content showed, the commands you ran with results and measured numbers, and anything not done or needing a decision.`

const SITE = `${COMMON}

You are the site and browser builder. You own website/build.py, website/templates/ (map.html: the two layer radios and the List view words; about.html: the bullet), website/static/map/map.js, website/static/map/map.css, tools/smoke_map.py, tests/test_site.py, and the small owned edit in website/swath.py and tests/test_swath.py that D15 names (describe() names Montana first; nothing else in the module changes). Build: (1) build.py: Collector.swath behind --storm-layers like the satellite (the two frames into the site's frames folder; the hail/live/<window>/<stamp>/ tile folders into the site; map.json["layers"]["hail_60"] and ["hail_1440"] from map_data_swath, including the live pattern with the stamp, the floor, fresh_min and stale_min, the valid time and every template; the status line "Hail swath (radar estimate)" in the List view and the no-JavaScript panel from describe; the page-side SAMPLE credit of D10 on sample builds); the default build (no --storm-layers) stays byte-identical to ${BASE} except shared static assets and their ?v= hashes; a --storm-layers build without --hail-history works (the layers draw; the sheet's live line needs --hail-history); a layer whose state is unavailable still builds, with its words; (2) templates: map.html gains the two radios under the weather layers with their words from map.json or the template, and the List view block; about.html the bullet with the contract's words; (3) map.js: two more one-frame layers exactly as the satellite layer (LAYER_WORD, HATCH for no coverage, titles, legend and source words from map.json); the view-time freshness of D7: the state line computed in the browser from the frame's valid time and the fresh_min and stale_min numbers in map.json, filled into the {age} templates, re-evaluated when the layer is switched on and once a minute while it is on, never from the build-time state field except as the initial value; the sheet's live line per D4, D5, D14 and D16: when a hail layer is on and the sheet opens for a cell, fetch the tile's live file from the pattern (the tile name from the same cell-to-tile arithmetic the sheet already uses), one fetch per window per click, cached by stamp; a 404 is the no-estimate line when the view-time state is fresh or stale and the unavailable line otherwise; another error is the could-not-be-loaded sentence from map.json and never a console error; the no-coverage cells of the tile's nocov list give the no-coverage sentence; document both duties in the header; no literal threshold, word, unit or window length in map.js (a test greps for the brief's words and numbers); (4) map.css: nothing new unless the legend needs it (say so); (5) tools/smoke_map.py: switch to each hail layer; the legend words present with every class colour and the uncoloured sentence; the pixel-change gate (the frame changes the picture by more than 2 percent of pixels when the live file has values in the box, else the note "no values in the box: pixel gate not applicable"); the state line with the view-time age; the sheet's live line on a cell with a value (find one from the live files of the build; skip with a note when none) and the no-estimate line on a cell without; the 404 path on a tile with no file; zero off-site requests; --shots at 390x844 and 1280x800; (6) tests/test_site.py: the flag plumbing, the identity check against ${BASE}, the map.js literal scan, the templates with and without --storm-layers, the List view words from a fixture frame, the SAMPLE credit; (7) the D15 words edit in swath.py with its test (the Montana-first sentence and the outside-Montana sentence; the nearest town never computed for a cell outside Montana; the forbidden-term test still passes). Build and check: ${VENV} -m unittest tests.test_site tests.test_swath; builds: default --sample --now 2026-10-19T12:00:00Z into ${OUT}/site/off (compare with the same build from a copy of the base: git -C ${WT} archive ${BASE} | tar -x -C ${OUT}/site/base-src); --storm-layers --sample into ${OUT}/site/sample; --storm-layers --hail-history --sample --hail-store ${STORE_TAR} into ${OUT}/site/real-sample; and a live build --storm-layers --hail-history --hail-store ${STORE_TAR} --require-live into ${OUT}/site/live (the other storm layers pull live too; allow 10 minutes; if a non-hail storm layer fails live, build without --require-live and say which source failed) and PW_CHROMIUM=/opt/pw-browsers/chromium ${VENV} tools/smoke_map.py --shots on it. Report what you changed and measured, the per-click fetch list, and the header text you added.`

const DOCS = `${COMMON}

You are the docs builder. You own docs/DECISIONS.md, docs/DESIGN.md, docs/ROADMAP.md, README.md, AGENTS.md, research/globe/README.md (the P3 row of section 6 only) and research/globe/validation-evidence/p3-verification.json (new). Write: D37 "Live hail swath layers on the Map, the globe plan's P3 (2026-10-19)" after D36: the owner decisions it serves (2, 4, 5, 6 by number from D34), the two products with their cadences and the verified units and codes (the table rows 209/3/30 and 209/3/34: mm, -1 missing, -3 no coverage; the files hold no zeros, so -1 is uncoloured and -3 hatched, D1), the valid time rule (D2), the file choice (D3), the live per-tile files in stamped folders and the sheet line (D4, D5, D13, D14), the freshness thresholds and why (D6, the measured publication lags), the view-time freshness in the browser (D7), the floor and the class words shared with B1, the Montana-first words (D15) and the 404 rule (D16), the words' honesty rules (a radar estimate, not observed hail, not damage; uncoloured is not "no hail"; "This is not an all-clear"), the reuse of the satellite layer pattern, the measured sizes from the module re-checks (PNG about 3 KB on a quiet day; live tiles a few hundred bytes; sample no-coverage tiles about 1.2 KB each), and *Why:* in the house style. DESIGN.md section 11: the two layers (colours by class word, hatch for no coverage, the uncoloured sentence), the List view block, the sheet's live line and its states, the data contract additions, the browser duties. ROADMAP: Next 11 moved to Done with "measured in the re-check" where numbers are pending; the open item that the picture box reaches into Canada and the D15 words. research/globe/README.md: the P3 row of section 6 updated to built-behind-the-flag with the date (that one row only). README and AGENTS: swath.py in the layout line. The verification record research/globe/validation-evidence/p3-verification.json with gates B4-1 to B4-7: the module gates B4-1, B4-2, B4-4 and B4-5 filled from ${OUT}/b4a-recheck.json and ${OUT}/b4a-recheck-completion.json with their measurements and the four module run times for B4-2, and B4-3, B4-6 and B4-7 pending until the site re-check. Em-dashes 0 in your lines; no model, AI-vendor or AI-product names; no invented measurements; quotes exact. Read the site builder's map.js header and smoke changes as they appear (poll every 5 minutes up to 60 minutes) so DESIGN's browser duties match. Report the diff stat of your files.`

const FINDINGS = { type: 'object', properties: { findings: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: { id: { type: 'string' }, file: { type: 'string' }, line: { type: 'integer' }, claim: { type: 'string' }, evidence: { type: 'string' }, fix: { type: 'string' }, severity: { type: 'string', enum: ['blocking', 'should', 'minor'] }, confidence: { type: 'number' } }, required: ['id', 'file', 'line', 'claim', 'evidence', 'fix', 'severity', 'confidence'] } }, measurements: { type: 'object', additionalProperties: true }, gates: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: { gate: { type: 'string' }, status: { type: 'string', enum: ['pass', 'fail', 'not_checked'] }, evidence: { type: 'string' } }, required: ['gate', 'status', 'evidence'] } }, summary: { type: 'string' } }, required: ['findings', 'measurements', 'gates', 'summary'] }
const VERDICT = { type: 'object', properties: { id: { type: 'string' }, defect_real: { type: 'boolean' }, refuted: { type: 'boolean' }, severity: { type: 'string', enum: ['blocking', 'should', 'minor'] }, reason: { type: 'string' }, fix_ok: { type: 'boolean' }, adjusted_fix: { type: 'string' } }, required: ['id', 'defect_real', 'refuted', 'severity', 'reason', 'fix_ok', 'adjusted_fix'] }

const REVIEW_COMMON = `Read-only reviewer in ${WT} (branch claude/hail-b4, based on ${BASE} for this part). Read ${BRIEF} first (the contract, gates B4-1 to B4-7, the pre-check facts, decisions D1 to D16, the part B list, the north star), then decisions 1 to 16 of ${B1BRIEF}. The module re-checks are ${OUT}/b4a-recheck.json and ${OUT}/b4a-recheck-completion.json; the downloaded files are in ${CACHE}/ and the pre-check scripts in ${PRECHECK}/. Never edit, stage, commit or push; scratch only under ${OUT}/<your-name>/ which you create; never delete anything outside it. Report concrete defects only, each with file, line, evidence (command output or quoted text) and an exact minimal fix; rank blocking first; a word without its unit or kind word, or a sentence that needs decoding, is a real finding; fill the gates you checked; put every measured number in measurements.`
const REVIEWERS = [
  { key: 'browser', prompt: `${REVIEW_COMMON} Lens: the site in Chromium (rule 8) and readability. Build from a copy of the worktree (cp -r without .git into ${OUT}/browser/src): default --sample --now 2026-10-19T12:00:00Z into ${OUT}/browser/off; --storm-layers --sample into ${OUT}/browser/sample; --storm-layers --hail-history --sample --hail-store ${STORE_TAR} into ${OUT}/browser/real-sample; a live build --storm-layers --hail-history --hail-store ${STORE_TAR} --require-live into ${OUT}/browser/live (allow 10 minutes; if a non-hail storm layer fails live, build without --require-live and say which source failed); and from the base (git -C ${WT} archive ${BASE} | tar -x -C ${OUT}/browser/base-src) the default build into ${OUT}/browser/base-off; diff -rq base-off vs off: only static/map/map.js, static/map/map.css and ?v= lines in pages may differ. Serve the live build and with Playwright (PW_CHROMIUM=/opt/pw-browsers/chromium; read tools/smoke_map.py for the harness) run tools/smoke_map.py --shots and quote the result; then your probes: switch to Hail, last hour and Hail, last 24 hours: the legend shows every class colour with its word and the uncoloured sentence of D1; the state line shows the valid time in Montana time and the fresh, stale or unavailable words with the view-time age (advance the page clock with Playwright's clock API or a shim and check the state changes at the fresh_min and stale_min thresholds from map.json); the pixel-change gate on each layer (or the not-applicable note); open the sheet on a cell listed in a live file (find one in the build's hail/live/ files; if none, on the sample build) and check the live line's inches, millimetres, class word and time; a cell with no value gives D5's line; a tile with no file gives the no-estimate line on a fresh layer and the unavailable line when you force the state stale-plus (D16); a no-coverage cell on the sample build gives the no-coverage sentence; every request stays on-site and the per-click fetch list is small (list it; one live fetch per window per click, cached); the List view and the no-JavaScript panel (JavaScript disabled) carry the words of the Product section with the Montana-first sentence (D15); the SAMPLE credit on sample builds; screenshots at 390x844 and 1280x800, light and dark, into ${OUT}/browser/shots; open them and describe (legend legible, hatch distinguishable, the layer not hiding the hail key or the search box); smoke_pages on the live build; read map.js's new code and list any literal threshold, word, unit or window length (none expected; formatting constants allowed).` },
  { key: 'rules', prompt: `${REVIEW_COMMON} Lens: repository rules and words over the whole diff of this part (git -C ${WT} diff ${BASE} --stat, the full diff, untracked files). Check: Python first (every viewer word in Python; the browser switches, fetches, computes the age from map.json numbers and fills); evidence honesty (every colour carries its word; "not observed hail", "not damage" and "This is not an all-clear" where the brief puts them; uncoloured never reads as "no hail"; nothing about damage, insurance, eligibility, confirmed hail; the forbidden-term check covers every new template); the contract row still matches the decode and the brief; tests exist for every behaviour change and ${VENV} -m unittest discover -s tests passes (quote the tail) and python desktop/launcher.py --selftest payload passes; website.yml runs tests.test_swath and the YAML parses; docs match what was built (D37, DESIGN 11, ROADMAP, README, AGENTS, the P3 row, p3-verification.json make no unmeasured claim and quote the re-check numbers exactly); em-dashes in added lines 0; the words Claude, Anthropic, Codex, ChatGPT, OpenAI, Copilot, Gemini, the worker model, the larger model, the mid model in added lines only inside branch names; plain wording and sentence case; no new pip package; decision 7 audit: every rmtree, unlink or os.remove under tests/ acts on a folder the test created; swath.py changed only in describe's words for D15 (diff it against ${BASE}).` },
  { key: 'live', prompt: `${REVIEW_COMMON} Lens: the live path inside the 10-minute site rebuild. (1) Time the whole --storm-layers --require-live build in your scratch (cp -r the worktree without .git) from an empty cache and with a warm cache; compare with the Website workflow's timeout and the 10-minute cadence (the build must leave margin: say how much); the swath step alone (listing, download, decode, PNG, live files for both products); (2) the request behaviour: user agent, retries, the ledger lines, one download per product per build, the cache key, and that the site build copies only the current stamp's folders; (3) the day boundary: with a fake clock at 00:01 UTC the listing falls back to yesterday's folder (D3); (4) the freshness thresholds against the lags you measure now (list the newest keys and compare their times with the current time, three times five minutes apart, for both products); (5) the failure paths end in state unavailable with the plain reason and the words carry "This is not an all-clear"; --require-live treats a failed hail swath as the satellite's failure is treated (check build.py and report which it follows); (6) the sizes: PNG bytes per layer (gate B4-5 under 150 KB), live files bytes and count today, the site's total growth against the base build; (7) the browser's view-time state: with the live build served, read map.json's valid, fresh_min and stale_min and confirm the state line's age in the page equals now minus valid to the minute.` },
]

const OWNERSHIP = {
  site: ['website/build.py', 'website/templates/', 'website/static/map/map.js', 'website/static/map/map.css', 'tools/smoke_map.py', 'tools/smoke_pages.py', 'tests/test_site.py', 'website/sources.py', '.github/workflows/website.yml'],
  swath: ['website/swath.py', 'tests/test_swath.py', 'website/gridded.py', 'website/sample.py'],
  docs: ['docs/', 'README.md', 'AGENTS.md', 'research/globe/'],
}
function ownerOf(file) {
  for (const [k, prefixes] of Object.entries(OWNERSHIP)) if (prefixes.some((p) => file.startsWith(p) || file.includes(p))) return k
  return 'site'
}

phase('Build')
const builds = await parallel([
  () => agent(SITE, { label: 'build:site-browser', phase: 'Build', model: WORKER }),
  () => agent(DOCS, { label: 'build:docs', phase: 'Build', model: WORKER }),
])
const [siteR, docsR] = builds
log(`builders done: site ${siteR ? 'ok' : 'none'}, docs ${docsR ? 'ok' : 'none'}`)

phase('Review')
const reports = `Builder reports for context (claims to check, not facts):\nSITE: ${(siteR || 'none').slice(0, 6000)}\nDOCS: ${(docsR || 'none').slice(0, 3000)}`
const reviews = await pipeline(
  REVIEWERS,
  (r) => agent(`${r.prompt}\n\n${reports}`, { label: `review:${r.key}`, phase: 'Review', model: WORKER, schema: FINDINGS }).then((result) => ({ r, result })),
  async ({ r, result }) => {
    if (!result) return { key: r.key, findings: [], gates: [], measurements: {}, summary: 'no result' }
    const fs = result.findings.map((f, i) => ({ ...f, id: `${r.key}-${i + 1}` }))
    const verdicts = await parallel(fs.map((f) => () =>
      agent(`Skeptic in ${WT} (branch claude/hail-b4; read-only; scratch only under ${OUT}/skeptic-${f.id}/; never edit, stage, commit or push; never delete outside your folder). Read the parts of ${BRIEF} the finding touches (decisions D1 to D16, the gates, the part B list). A finding is a defect if the code, the build output or the words behave as the finding says and that behaviour breaks a rule of the brief, a repository rule (AGENTS.md: evidence honesty, Python first, feed contracts, tests with every behaviour change, plain wording, real-browser checks) or the north star (a word without its unit or kind word; a sentence that needs decoding). Reproduce it yourself (run the code, build, open the page in Chromium if needed, read the output). Set defect_real true when the defect exists, even if the finding's framing, severity or fix is wrong; set refuted true only when the behaviour does not occur or is allowed by the brief or a decision you cite. Judge the fix: fix_ok, or an adjusted_fix.\n\nFinding ${f.id} (${f.severity}): ${f.file}:${f.line}. Claim: ${f.claim}. Evidence: ${f.evidence}. Proposed fix: ${f.fix}`, { label: `verify:${f.id}`, phase: 'Verify', model: WORKER, schema: VERDICT })))
    return { key: r.key, findings: fs.map((f, i) => ({ ...f, verdict: verdicts[i] || { id: f.id, defect_real: true, refuted: false, severity: f.severity, reason: 'no verdict', fix_ok: true, adjusted_fix: '' } })), gates: result.gates, measurements: result.measurements, summary: result.summary }
  }
)
const all = reviews.filter(Boolean).flatMap((r) => r.findings)
const confirmed = all.filter((f) => f.verdict.defect_real && !f.verdict.refuted).map((f) => ({ id: f.id, file: f.file, line: f.line, claim: f.claim, evidence: f.evidence, severity: f.verdict.severity || f.severity, fix: f.verdict.fix_ok ? f.fix : (f.verdict.adjusted_fix || f.fix), owner: ownerOf(f.file) }))
const refuted = all.filter((f) => !f.verdict.defect_real || f.verdict.refuted).map((f) => ({ id: f.id, file: f.file, claim: f.claim, reason: f.verdict.reason }))
log(`confirmed ${confirmed.length} (blocking ${confirmed.filter((f) => f.severity === 'blocking').length}), refuted ${refuted.length}`)

phase('Fix')
const FIX_DECISIONS = `SUPERVISOR DECISIONS: the brief ${BRIEF} carries decisions D1 to D16 and any later numbered decisions; read them in full before applying any finding and apply the findings in their light (a finding that asks for a choice is decided there; a finding that contradicts a decision is skipped with the decision cited).`
const groups = ['site', 'swath', 'docs'].map((k) => ({ k, items: confirmed.filter((f) => f.owner === k) })).filter((g) => g.items.length)
const fixReports = await parallel(groups.map((g) => () =>
  agent(`${COMMON}\n\n${FIX_DECISIONS}\n\nYou are the ${g.k} fixer; you own ${OWNERSHIP[g.k].join(', ')}. Apply these confirmed findings exactly (the adjusted fix where given), add or update a test for each behaviour change, run ${VENV} -m unittest tests.test_site tests.test_swath tests.test_gridded tests.test_storm (quote the tail), and for a browser change rebuild ${OUT}/site/real-sample and re-run tools/smoke_map.py on it (PW_CHROMIUM=/opt/pw-browsers/chromium). Findings:\n${g.items.map((f) => `- ${f.id} [${f.severity}] ${f.file}:${f.line}: ${f.claim}. Fix: ${f.fix}`).join('\n')}\n\nReport each finding as applied, already fixed or skipped with the reason.`, { label: `fix:${g.k}`, phase: 'Fix', model: WORKER })))

phase('Recheck')
const recheck = await agent(`${REVIEW_COMMON} ${FIX_DECISIONS} You are the final checker. Run and quote: ${VENV} -m unittest discover -s tests (tail); python desktop/launcher.py --selftest payload; builds from a copy of the worktree (cp -r without .git into ${OUT}/recheck/src): the default build against the base ${BASE} build (diff -rq; only map.js, map.css and ?v= lines may differ), --storm-layers --sample, --storm-layers --hail-history --sample with ${STORE_TAR}, and the live build --storm-layers --hail-history --hail-store ${STORE_TAR} --require-live (allow 10 minutes; say which source failed if one did); serve the live build and run PW_CHROMIUM=/opt/pw-browsers/chromium ${VENV} tools/smoke_map.py --shots (quote the result) and smoke_pages; your own probes in Chromium: the two layers' legend words, the view-time state line and its change at the thresholds, the sheet's live line on a cell with a value and the no-estimate line on one without, the 404 path, the no-coverage sentence on the sample build, the per-click fetch list (one live fetch per window per click), zero off-site requests, the List view and no-JavaScript words with the Montana-first sentence, the SAMPLE credit; the YAML parses; git -C ${WT} status --short and diff --stat ${BASE}; em-dash and banned-name counts over added lines; the map.js literal scan; the decision 7 audit; the docs against the build (D37, DESIGN 11, ROADMAP, README, AGENTS, the P3 row, p3-verification.json: every number traced to a re-check). Write ${OUT}/b4b-recheck.json with gates B4-1 to B4-7 (status, evidence; B4-2 cites the four module run times), every part B item done or not done, the measurements and the open items. Return that JSON as text and name every check that failed.`, { label: 'recheck', phase: 'Recheck', model: WORKER })

return {
  siteR: (siteR || '').slice(0, 5000), docsR: (docsR || '').slice(0, 3000),
  reviews: reviews.filter(Boolean).map((r) => ({ key: r.key, summary: r.summary, gates: r.gates, measurements: r.measurements })),
  confirmed, refuted,
  fixes: fixReports.map((r) => (r || '').slice(0, 3000)),
  recheck,
}
